perspective:
I, Angela Hwang, have access to the following information:

- I am Angela Hwang, a hairdresser with a doctorate. Kevin Flores has been my close friend since high school; we confide in each other. He works as a construction worker.
- I invited Kevin to coffee because I noticed he seemed unhappy with his job.
- At coffee, Kevin told me he was “alright, just the usual grind,” then admitted he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was just going through the motions. He had thought about changing jobs/careers but did not know where to start and felt overwhelmed.
- I offered to figure out options with him and look into possibilities. Kevin agreed and thanked me.
- Later, I found job openings and a career counseling service and shared them with Kevin. He thanked me and said he had been thinking about something more creative, maybe design or architecture. I encouraged him to check the resources, and he said he would.
- I believed Kevin was hesitant, felt frustrated and worried, and arranged a meeting with a career coach. When I told him, Kevin said I didn’t have to, appreciated it, but wasn’t sure he was ready. I encouraged him; he agreed to give it a shot.
- I checked in about the career coach. Kevin told me the coach was helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident. I told him I was proud and offered more help.
- I believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career. I organized a small celebration party for him. Kevin thanked me and said he couldn’t have done it without me; I told him he did the hard work and we should celebrate.

No hidden facts about Kevin’s private thoughts, narrator-only traits, or events I did not observe/hear are available to me.
